1.explanation: The accessibility violation originates in the Breadcrumb skeleton implementation. Breadcrumb.Skeleton.js emits link elements with no accessible name or alt text, which fails WCAG requirements. To fix it, you must update Breadcrumb.Skeleton.js (for example, replace <a> with <div> or add aria-hidden and non-interactive markup) so that no empty links are rendered. The accompanying test in Breadcrumb.Skeleton-test.js will also need to be updated to reflect the corrected markup and snapshot changes.
1.bug_scenario: When you load the Breadcrumb “skeleton” component in React and run the IBM DAP ruleset against it, each breadcrumb segment is rendered as a bare link with no visible text or alt text. The DAP report flags every breadcrumb link with “Hyperlink is missing link text or an image with alt text,” because the skeleton mark-up uses empty <a> tags (or Link wrappers) purely as visual placeholders.

2.explanation: Breadcrumb.Skeleton.js is responsible for rendering the skeleton UI of the Breadcrumb component. In its current implementation it creates anchor elements for each placeholder breadcrumb item without any text content or aria-label, which triggers the DAP violation. Updating this file to either remove the <a> wrapper for skeleton items or add an appropriate aria-label (or hidden text) for each link will resolve the missing hyperlink label error.
2.bug_scenario: The skeleton variant of the React Breadcrumb component is rendering breadcrumb items as hyperlinks (<a> tags) that contain only visual placeholders and no actual link text or image alt text. Running the IBM DAP accessibility ruleset flags each breadcrumb item with “Hyperlinks must contain link text or an image with alt text,” because these placeholder links have no accessible label.
